metadata.name: English Learning Topic Bank
metadata.description: Hard-coded topic bank for an English learning app. TOEIC 4 skills and IELTS Speaking/Writing. IELTS Writing sections include real reported exam questions (2025-2026) and predicted trending topics, graded from easy to hard via the per-topic level field.

contentSources.name: IELTS.org (British Council / IDP / Cambridge) — official sample test questions
contentSources.usedFor: Official task formats, letter types, and map/process task modelling

contentSources.name: Take IELTS (British Council) — free practice tests
contentSources.usedFor: Letter register conventions and General Training task modelling

contentSources.name: IELTS Liz — speaking topics 2026
contentSources.usedFor: Speaking Part 1 topics and recurring essay themes

contentSources.name: Simply IELTS — confirmed speaking topics and Task 1 quarterly reviews (2026)
contentSources.usedFor: Reported real Speaking Part 1/2 topics and Academic Task 1 chart questions

contentSources.name: AllThingsIELTS — speaking topics and 50 cue cards 2026
IELTS Datio — IELTS Speaking Q3 2026 forecast
contentSources.usedFor: Reported Speaking Part 2 cue card forecast (Forecast Q3 2026 topic group)

contentSources.name: IELTSPodcast — 250+ recent Task 2 questions
contentSources.usedFor: Reported real Writing Task 2 essay questions

contentSources.name: IELTSMaterial — recent Task 2 topics 2025
contentSources.usedFor: Reported real Writing Task 2 essay questions

contentSources.name: Cathoven — topic forecasts 2026
contentSources.usedFor: Predicted trending topics (generative AI, four-day week, cost of living)

contentSources.name: Writing9 — Task 1 and Task 2 topic banks
contentSources.usedFor: Academic Task 1 table topics and General letter scenarios

contentSources.name: IELTS Buddy — latest writing topics
contentSources.usedFor: General Task 1 letter scenarios and essay themes

contentSources.name: How to do IELTS — Task 1 bank

recommendedUsage: Use topics as fixed seeds in the app.
Let AI generate dynamic questions, model answers, feedback, vocabulary, and rubrics from each topic.
Teachers can filter by exam, skill, section, level, and taskType.

photoLinkStrategy.prototype: Photo-based topics contain direct imageUrl and thumbnailUrl fields.
photoLinkStrategy.production: Replace dynamic placeholder URLs with selected licensed images and cache them in your own CDN/storage.
photoLinkStrategy.note: Unsplash Source-style dynamic URLs are avoided because that endpoint has been deprecated for new projects.

samplePrompts: Create an IELTS Academic Writing Task 1 question with two pie charts comparing Australian household energy use (heating, cooling, water heating, appliances, lighting) in 1995 and 2015. Include realistic percentages, an outline, and a model answer.
Write a model Band 6.5 answer comparing the two pie charts, highlighting the biggest changes between the two years.
List comparison vocabulary for describing proportions and changes between two time periods.
teacherNotes: Difficulty: Easy — two pie charts with the same categories are the most accessible Task 1 type.
Focus on selecting the 3-4 most significant changes, not describing every segment.
Practise the language of proportion: 'accounted for', 'made up', 'a quarter of', 'the largest share'.

topics.topicName: Table comparing average weekly working hours in five different countries in 2010 and 2025
topics.description: IELTS Task 1 Academic — Table comparison: weekly working hours across five countries.
topics.source: Modelled on recurring table questions — writing9.com Task 1 table topic bank
samplePrompts: Create an IELTS Academic Writing Task 1 question with a table comparing average weekly working hours in five countries in 2010 and 2025. Include realistic figures, an outline, and a model answer.
Write a model Band 6.5 answer selecting and grouping the most notable figures from the table.
List vocabulary for describing rises, falls, and stability in numerical data.
teacherNotes: Difficulty: Easy — tables with two time points train grouping and selection skills.
Encourage grouping countries by trend (increased vs decreased) instead of listing row by row.
Overview should state the general direction of change and the highest/lowest values.

topics.topicName: Line graph showing the number of overseas tourists (in millions) who visited France, Spain and Japan between 1990 and 2020
topics.description: IELTS Task 1 Academic — Line graph reported in real 2026 exams: overseas tourists in three countries over 30 years.
topics.source: Reported real exam question (Q1 2026) — compiled by simplyielts.com
samplePrompts: Create an IELTS Academic Writing Task 1 question with a line graph showing overseas tourist numbers for France, Spain and Japan from 1990 to 2020. Include realistic figures, an outline, and a model answer.
Write a model Band 7 answer comparing the three trends, including a clear overview of the overall pattern.
List trend vocabulary for long time periods: 'climbed steadily', 'peaked at', 'dipped', 'plateaued'.
teacherNotes: Difficulty: Medium — three lines over 30 years require selective comparison.
The 2020 endpoint typically shows a sharp fall (pandemic) — a key feature for the overview.
Practise comparative structures: 'while France remained the most visited, Japan grew the fastest'.

topics.topicName: Bar chart comparing renewable energy consumption (solar, wind and hydro) in four European countries in 2015 and 2025
topics.description: IELTS Task 1 Academic — Bar chart reported in real 2026 exams: renewable energy in four European countries.
topics.source: Reported real exam question (2026) — compiled by ielts.preptical.com and examword.com
samplePrompts: Create an IELTS Academic Writing Task 1 question with a grouped bar chart comparing solar, wind and hydro energy consumption in four European countries in 2015 and 2025. Include realistic figures, an outline, and a model answer.
Write a model Band 7 answer organising the data by country group and by energy type.
List vocabulary for comparing categories: 'by far the largest', 'roughly double', 'a marginal increase'.
teacherNotes: Difficulty: Medium — two grouping dimensions (country × energy type) test organisation skills.
Two valid organisation strategies: paragraph per year, or paragraph per energy type.
Warn against mechanical listing — the response must compare, not just report.

topics.topicName: A bar chart showing the number of international students enrolled in universities in three countries between 2005 and 2025, together with a line graph showing average tuition fees over the same period
topics.description: IELTS Task 1 Academic — Multi-chart task (bar + line): international student enrolment and tuition fees. Multi-graph tasks appeared in about a quarter of Q1 2026 tests.
topics.source: Reported real exam trend (Q1 2026) — simplyielts.com quarterly review
samplePrompts: Create an IELTS Academic Writing Task 1 multi-chart question combining a bar chart (international student enrolment in three countries, 2005-2025) with a line graph (average tuition fees). Include realistic figures, an outline, and a model answer.
Write a model Band 7.5 answer that connects the two charts in the overview and compares trends across both.
List linking phrases for relating two data sets: 'despite rising fees', 'this growth coincided with', 'in contrast to'.
teacherNotes: Difficulty: Hard — two related charts require synthesis, the most demanding Task 1 skill.
The overview must mention BOTH charts and ideally the relationship between them.
Time management is critical: students often overwrite on chart one and rush chart two.

topics.topicName: Two maps showing a coastal town centre in 2000 and the present day, with changes to roads, buildings and public spaces
topics.description: IELTS Task 1 Academic — Map comparison: changes to a town centre over time. Maps are a recurring high-difficulty Task 1 type.
topics.source: Recurring official task type — ielts.org sample questions and howtodoielts.com Task 1 bank
samplePrompts: Create an IELTS Academic Writing Task 1 map-comparison question describing changes to a coastal town centre between 2000 and now (new roads, demolished buildings, converted spaces). Include an outline and a model answer.
Write a model Band 7.5 answer using the language of spatial change and passive voice.
List map vocabulary: 'was demolished', 'was converted into', 'to the north of', 'replaced by', 'pedestrianised'.
teacherNotes: Difficulty: Hard — maps require spatial language and heavy use of the passive voice.
Organise by area of the map or by type of change, never feature by feature at random.
The overview should summarise the overall transformation, e.g. 'the centre became more commercial and pedestrian-friendly'.

topics.topicName: Pie chart and bar chart showing how households in three countries divided their monthly spending between housing, food, transport and leisure in 2025
topics.description: IELTS Task 1 Academic — Mixed pie and bar chart: household spending across three countries.
topics.source: Modelled on recurring mixed-chart questions — writing9.com Task 1 topic bank
samplePrompts: Create an IELTS Academic Writing Task 1 question combining a pie chart and a bar chart on household spending (housing, food, transport, leisure) in three countries in 2025. Include realistic percentages, an outline, and a model answer.
Write a model Band 7 answer that selects key contrasts between the countries rather than describing every figure.
List vocabulary for proportions and cross-country comparison: 'the lion's share', 'comparable to', 'twice as much as'.
teacherNotes: Difficulty: Medium — two chart types but one familiar theme keeps the synthesis manageable.
Group by spending category or by country; do not alternate randomly.
The overview should name the dominant spending category and the most divergent country.

topics.topicName: Process diagram showing how electricity is generated in a hydroelectric power station
topics.description: IELTS Task 1 Academic — Process diagram: hydroelectric power generation. A recurring real-exam process task.
topics.source: Recurring real exam task — howtodoielts.com Task 1 bank and Cambridge IELTS practice tests
samplePrompts: Create an IELTS Academic Writing Task 1 process-diagram question describing how a hydroelectric power station generates electricity (dam, reservoir, turbine, generator, power lines). Include an outline and a model answer.
Write a model Band 7.5 answer using sequencing language and the passive voice throughout.
List process vocabulary: 'is channelled through', 'drives the turbine', 'is converted into', 'subsequently', 'at the final stage'.
teacherNotes: Difficulty: Hard — man-made processes demand passive voice, sequencing, and technical paraphrase.
There are no trends in a process task — the overview states the number of stages and the start and end points.
Students must paraphrase the diagram labels, not copy them verbatim.

topics.topicName: Diagram showing the life cycle of a salmon, from egg to adult fish returning to the river
topics.description: IELTS Task 1 Academic — Natural process: the salmon life cycle. Reported in real exams and Cambridge practice materials.
topics.source: Reported real exam task — Cambridge IELTS series; compiled by howtodoielts.com
samplePrompts: Create an IELTS Academic Writing Task 1 natural-process question describing the life cycle of a salmon (eggs in the river, fry, juvenile in lakes, adult at sea, return to spawn). Include an outline and a model answer.
Write a model Band 7.5 answer using present simple active voice and clear cyclical sequencing.
List life-cycle vocabulary: 'hatch into', 'migrate downstream', 'mature', 'return to spawn', 'the cycle begins anew'.
teacherNotes: Difficulty: Hard — natural cycles use ACTIVE voice, unlike man-made processes; students often mix this up.
A cyclical process has no true end — the overview should mention that the cycle repeats.
Time spans at each stage (months, years) are key details worth including.

topics.topicName: Table and line graph showing water consumption by sector (agriculture, industry, domestic) in two regions between 2000 and 2025
topics.description: IELTS Task 1 Academic — Multi-chart task (table + line graph): water consumption by sector across two regions.
topics.source: Modelled on Q1 2026 multi-chart exam trend — simplyielts.com quarterly review
samplePrompts: Create an IELTS Academic Writing Task 1 multi-chart question combining a table (water use by sector in two regions) with a line graph (total consumption 2000-2025). Include realistic figures, an outline, and a model answer.
Write a model Band 7.5 answer connecting the sector breakdown to the overall trend.
List vocabulary for resource data: 'accounts for the bulk of', 'a steady upward trajectory', 'consumption per capita'.
teacherNotes: Difficulty: Hard — combining a snapshot table with a 25-year trend tests selection and synthesis.
The overview must connect both charts: which sector dominates AND how the total has changed.
Warn against describing all table cells — pick the highest, the lowest, and the biggest change.

topics.topicName:
You have recently moved to a new city and would like your friend to visit you.

Write a letter to your friend. In your letter:
• describe your new home
• explain what you like about the city
• suggest some activities you can do together
topics.description: IELTS General Writing Task 1 — Informal Letter. Inviting a friend to visit your new city.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS General Writing Task 1 Informal Letter. Check that all three bullet points are fully addressed, the register is appropriately informal (friendly, personal tone), and the letter is organised with a suitable opening and closing. Give a band score and feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 informal letter of around 160 words. Use a friendly tone, contractions, and informal phrases. Cover all three bullet points.
List 10 useful informal phrases and expressions for inviting a friend and describing a new home.
teacherNotes: Letter type: Informal — students should use a warm, personal tone (Hi/Hey [Name], contractions, exclamations).
All three bullet points must be addressed: home description, city highlights, and specific activity suggestions.
Common error: switching to formal language mid-letter. Reinforce consistent informal register throughout.

topics.topicName:
A friend invited you to a birthday party, but you were unable to attend.

Write a letter to your friend. In your letter:
• apologise for missing the party
• explain why you could not attend
• suggest a time to meet your friend
topics.description: IELTS General Writing Task 1 — Informal Letter. Apologising for missing a birthday party.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS General Writing Task 1 Informal Letter apologising for missing a party. Check register, bullet point coverage, and organisation. Give a band score and feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 informal letter of around 160 words apologising and suggesting a meeting time.
List useful informal phrases for apologising, giving excuses, and suggesting plans with a friend.
teacherNotes: Letter type: Informal — tone must be warm and genuine, not stiff or overly formal.
Key language focus: expressing regret (I am so sorry I missed..., I felt terrible about...) and making suggestions (How about we meet...?).
Students often write too short apologies. Encourage them to expand on both the explanation and the invitation.

topics.topicName:
You are going away for a short holiday and would like a friend to take care of your home.

Write a letter to your friend. In your letter:
• explain when you will be away
• describe what you would like your friend to do
• tell your friend how to contact you during your trip
topics.description: IELTS General Writing Task 1 — Informal Letter. Asking a friend to house-sit.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS General Writing Task 1 Informal Letter asking a friend to look after a home. Give a band score and feedback on register, bullet point coverage, and cohesion.
Write a model Band 6.5 informal letter of around 160 words covering all three bullet points with a natural, friendly tone.
List useful informal phrases for making requests, giving instructions, and sharing contact details.
teacherNotes: Letter type: Informal — students must use a friendly, relaxed tone while being clear about the requests.
Bullet 2 (what to do) is often underdeveloped. Encourage specific tasks: watering plants, collecting post, feeding pets.
Bullet 3 must give a real means of contact (phone number, email) not just say "you can contact me".

topics.topicName:
A friend recently helped you prepare for an important event.

Write a letter to your friend. In your letter:
• thank your friend for the help
• explain how the event went
• invite your friend to do something together
topics.description: IELTS General Writing Task 1 — Informal Letter. Thanking a friend for their help.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS General Writing Task 1 Informal Letter thanking a friend. Give a band score and feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 informal letter of around 160 words with warm thanks, a description of the event, and an invitation.
List useful phrases for expressing gratitude informally and describing a past event.
teacherNotes: Letter type: Informal — students should sound genuinely warm and personal, not formulaic.
Bullet 2 (how the event went) must be specific, not vague. Encourage details: outcome, how they felt, what went well.
Bullet 3 should include a specific suggestion (e.g., dinner this Saturday, a film next week).

topics.topicName:
Your friend is planning to visit your hometown and has asked for your advice.

Write a letter to your friend. In your letter:
• recommend a place to stay
• suggest some places to visit
• give advice about transport
topics.description: IELTS General Writing Task 1 — Informal Letter. Giving travel advice to a visiting friend.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS General Writing Task 1 Informal Letter giving travel advice. Give a band score and feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 informal letter of around 160 words with specific recommendations for accommodation, sightseeing, and getting around.
List useful informal phrases for giving recommendations, suggestions, and travel advice.
teacherNotes: Letter type: Informal — advice should feel friendly and enthusiastic, like a personal recommendation.
All three bullet points require specific details: actual place names or types, not vague suggestions.
Transport advice often missed: remind students to cover how to get from A to B (bus, taxi, walking distance).

topics.topicName:
You are taking an evening course, but you will be unable to attend several classes.

Write a letter to your teacher. In your letter:
• explain why you cannot attend the classes
• say how long you will be absent
• ask how you can keep up with the course
topics.description: IELTS General Writing Task 1 — Semi-formal Letter. Writing to a teacher about absence.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS General Writing Task 1 Semi-formal Letter to a teacher. Check that the tone is polite but not overly formal, all bullet points are addressed, and the letter is well-organised. Give a band score and feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 semi-formal letter of around 160 words to a teacher explaining an absence and asking how to catch up.
List useful semi-formal phrases for explaining absence, apologising, and requesting help from a teacher.
teacherNotes: Letter type: Semi-formal — tone should be respectful but warmer than a formal complaint letter (Dear Mr/Ms [Name], Regards).
Students often confuse formal and semi-formal register. Key difference: semi-formal uses the recipient name and a less rigid tone.
Bullet 3 is key: students must ask specifically how to catch up (missed notes, extra sessions, online materials).

topics.topicName:
Your neighbour frequently plays loud music late at night.

Write a letter to your neighbour. In your letter:
• explain how the noise affects you
• describe when the problem usually occurs
• suggest a possible solution
topics.description: IELTS General Writing Task 1 — Semi-formal Letter. Complaining to a neighbour about noise.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS General Writing Task 1 Semi-formal Letter to a neighbour about noise. Give a band score and feedback on tone, bullet point coverage, and language use.
Write a model Band 6.5 semi-formal letter of around 160 words that is firm but polite, covering all three bullet points.
List useful semi-formal phrases for making a complaint politely and suggesting a compromise.
teacherNotes: Letter type: Semi-formal — the tone must be polite but assertive, not aggressive or too casual.
Register challenge: students must NOT write "I am writing to complain..." (too formal) but also avoid "You always wake me up" (too informal/aggressive).
Bullet 3 must include a realistic, constructive suggestion (a quiet time after 10pm, using headphones, etc.).

topics.topicName:
You are considering changing your job and would like advice from a former colleague.

Write a letter to your former colleague. In your letter:
• explain why you are thinking about changing jobs
• describe the type of job you are looking for
• ask for advice or useful contacts
topics.description: IELTS General Writing Task 1 — Semi-formal Letter. Asking a former colleague for career advice.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS General Writing Task 1 Semi-formal Letter asking for career advice. Give a band score and feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 semi-formal letter of around 160 words to a former colleague asking for job advice and contacts.
List useful semi-formal phrases for explaining career decisions and requesting advice or referrals.
teacherNotes: Letter type: Semi-formal — a former colleague is known but in a professional context, so avoid overly casual language.
Bullet 2 must be specific: what industry, role type, or skills the writer wants to use — not just "a better job".
Bullet 3: students should ask a specific question, not just "please give me advice".

topics.topicName:
You live in an apartment building and think that some improvements are needed.

Write a letter to the building manager. In your letter:
• describe the current problems
• explain how they affect the residents
• suggest some improvements
topics.description: IELTS General Writing Task 1 — Semi-formal Letter. Suggesting improvements to a building manager.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS General Writing Task 1 Semi-formal Letter to a building manager. Give a band score and feedback on register, bullet point coverage, and organisation.
Write a model Band 6.5 semi-formal letter of around 160 words politely describing problems and proposing practical improvements.
List useful semi-formal phrases for describing problems in a building and making polite suggestions to a manager.
teacherNotes: Letter type: Semi-formal — writing to a building manager requires respect but is not as formal as writing to a company CEO.
Problems should be specific: broken lift, poor lighting in hallways, no recycling bins, etc.
Students often write a formal complaint instead of a constructive improvement request — emphasise the suggestion focus.

topics.topicName:
You recently completed a course and found it very useful.

Write a letter to your teacher. In your letter:
• thank the teacher
• explain what you found useful about the course
• describe how the course may help you in the future
topics.description: IELTS General Writing Task 1 — Semi-formal Letter. Thanking a teacher after completing a course.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS General Writing Task 1 Semi-formal Letter thanking a teacher. Give a band score and feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 semi-formal letter of around 160 words expressing genuine gratitude and explaining the value of the course.
List useful semi-formal phrases for expressing gratitude, describing learning outcomes, and discussing future goals.
teacherNotes: Letter type: Semi-formal — warm and appreciative, but still professional (not a casual thank-you note to a friend).
Bullet 2 must identify specific content or skills from the course, not just say "everything was useful".
Bullet 3 should link the course to a realistic future goal (career, further study, daily life).

topics.topicName:
You recently bought an electronic device online, but it does not work properly.

Write a letter to the company. In your letter:
• describe the product and the problem
• explain what happened when you tried to use it
• say what you would like the company to do
topics.description: IELTS General Writing Task 1 — Formal Letter. Complaining about a faulty electronic device.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS General Writing Task 1 Formal Letter of complaint. Check for formal register throughout (Dear Sir/Madam, Yours faithfully), clear bullet point coverage, and appropriate complaint language. Give a band score and feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 formal complaint letter of around 160 words to a company about a faulty product.
List 10 useful formal phrases for writing a complaint letter, describing faults, and requesting action.
teacherNotes: Letter type: Formal — must use Dear Sir/Madam, Yours faithfully, no contractions, no casual language.
Bullet 3 must state a specific resolution: full refund, replacement, repair — not just "please fix it".
Register is frequently wrong here: students mix formal and informal phrases. Drill formal vocabulary explicitly.

topics.topicName:
You recently stayed at a hotel and were dissatisfied with the service.

Write a letter to the hotel manager. In your letter:
• explain when you stayed at the hotel
• describe the problems you experienced
• say what action you would like the manager to take
topics.description: IELTS General Writing Task 1 — Formal Letter. Complaining about hotel service.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS General Writing Task 1 Formal complaint letter about a hotel. Give a band score and feedback on formal register, bullet point coverage, and tone.
Write a model Band 6.5 formal letter of around 160 words complaining about hotel service and requesting compensation or an apology.
List useful formal phrases for hotel complaints and requesting specific actions from management.
teacherNotes: Letter type: Formal — even though a hotel manager may seem approachable, this is a business complaint and requires formal register.
Students should include specific dates and room details in Bullet 1 to make the letter credible and realistic.
Bullet 3: request must be concrete — compensation, partial refund, formal apology, written acknowledgement.

topics.topicName:
You are interested in taking a language course in another country.

Write a letter to the course provider. In your letter:
• explain why you are interested in the course
• ask about the schedule and fees
• ask about accommodation options
topics.description: IELTS General Writing Task 1 — Formal Letter. Requesting information about a language course abroad.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS General Writing Task 1 Formal Letter requesting course information. Give a band score and feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 formal inquiry letter of around 160 words covering all three bullet points clearly.
List useful formal phrases for inquiry letters: expressing interest, asking polite questions, and requesting information.
teacherNotes: Letter type: Formal — writing to an unknown organisation requires Dear Sir/Madam and Yours faithfully.
Bullets 2 and 3 require direct questions, but phrased politely (Could you please inform me...? I would be grateful if you could...).
Students often forget to state their purpose clearly in the opening paragraph before asking questions.

topics.topicName:
You have seen an advertisement for volunteers at a community event.

Write a letter to the organisers. In your letter:
• explain why you would like to volunteer
• describe your relevant skills or experience
• ask for more information about the work
topics.description: IELTS General Writing Task 1 — Formal Letter. Applying to volunteer at a community event.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS General Writing Task 1 Formal Letter applying for volunteer work. Give a band score and feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 formal volunteer application letter of around 160 words covering motivation, relevant experience, and a question about the role.
List useful formal phrases for expressing interest in volunteering and describing relevant skills.
teacherNotes: Letter type: Formal — organisers are unknown, so formal register is required throughout.
Bullet 2 is often weak: students should write specific skills or experiences, not just "I am hard-working and friendly".
Bullet 3 must ask a genuine clarifying question about the role (hours, location, training, dress code, etc.).

topics.topicName:
You recently experienced a problem while using public transport.

Write a letter to the transport company. In your letter:
• describe the journey
• explain what went wrong
• suggest how the service could be improved
topics.description: IELTS General Writing Task 1 — Formal Letter. Complaining about a public transport problem.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS General Writing Task 1 Formal Letter to a transport company. Give a band score and detailed feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 formal complaint and suggestion letter of around 160 words about a transport problem.
List useful formal phrases for describing travel incidents, expressing dissatisfaction, and proposing service improvements.
teacherNotes: Letter type: Formal — a transport company is an institution; formal register is required.
Bullet 1 must include specific journey details: route, date, time, ticket type — this makes the complaint credible.
Bullet 3 is often missed or vague. Remind students to offer a concrete, realistic improvement suggestion.

topics.topicName:
You have an appointment with an organisation but cannot attend at the arranged time.

Write a letter to the organisation. In your letter:
• explain why you cannot attend
• apologise for the inconvenience
• suggest another suitable time
topics.description: IELTS General Writing Task 1 — Formal Letter. Requesting to reschedule an appointment.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS General Writing Task 1 Formal Letter rescheduling an appointment. Give a band score and feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 formal letter of around 160 words politely explaining an absence and proposing a new appointment time.
List useful formal phrases for apologising for an inconvenience and proposing alternative arrangements.
teacherNotes: Letter type: Formal — writing to an unknown organisation requires formal register throughout.
Bullet 2 (apology) must sound sincere and formal, not casual: "I sincerely apologise for any inconvenience this may cause."
Bullet 3 must give two or three specific time options, not just say "whenever is convenient for you".

topics.topicName:
You left an important item at a hotel during a recent trip.

Write a letter to the hotel manager. In your letter:
• describe the item
• explain where you think you left it
• ask the hotel staff to send it to you if it is found
topics.description: IELTS General Writing Task 1 — Formal Letter. Reporting a lost item at a hotel.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS General Writing Task 1 Formal Letter about a lost item. Give a band score and feedback on formal register, accuracy of bullet point coverage, and clarity of request.
Write a model Band 6.5 formal letter of around 160 words describing the lost item and asking for it to be returned.
List useful formal phrases for describing a lost item, explaining circumstances, and making a polite request.
teacherNotes: Letter type: Formal — a hotel manager is an institution representative; formal register is required.
Bullet 1 must be very specific: colour, size, brand, distinguishing features — the more detail, the more realistic.
Bullet 3 must include the writer's postal address or instructions for how to return the item, not just "please send it back".

topics.topicName:
You are a member of a local gym and believe that some improvements are needed.

Write a letter to the gym manager. In your letter:
• describe the current problems
• explain how they affect members
• suggest some improvements
topics.description: IELTS General Writing Task 1 — Formal Letter. Suggesting gym improvements to the manager.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS General Writing Task 1 Formal Letter to a gym manager suggesting improvements. Give a band score and feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 formal letter of around 160 words identifying gym problems, their impact on members, and constructive improvement suggestions.
List useful formal phrases for describing facility problems, explaining their impact, and making polite suggestions to a manager.
teacherNotes: Letter type: Formal — even though the writer is a member (a client relationship), writing to a gym manager requires formal register.
Bullet 1: encourage specific problems (broken equipment, dirty changing rooms, overcrowding at peak times).
Bullet 3: improvements must directly address the problems raised, showing logical cause-and-effect thinking.

topics.topicName:
A friend from another country is visiting your town next month.

Write a letter to your friend. In your letter:
• say how you feel about the visit
• describe some places you will visit together
• suggest what your friend should bring
topics.description: IELTS General Writing Task 1 — Informal Letter. Welcoming a friend visiting your town.
topics.source: Modelled on official sample letters — takeielts.britishcouncil.org free practice tests
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS General Writing Task 1 Informal Letter welcoming a visiting friend. Give a band score and feedback on informal register and coverage of all three bullets.
Write a model Band 6.5 informal letter of around 160 words with warm, natural language and concrete plans.
List informal openings, closings, and friendly expressions for inviting and making plans.
teacherNotes: Difficulty: Easy — informal letters are the most accessible General Task 1 type.
Register must be consistently informal: contractions, phrasal verbs, friendly tone.
Each bullet needs development — one or two sentences per bullet, not a single word.

topics.topicName:
There is a problem with the heating system in the flat you rent, and the landlord has not responded to your phone calls.

Write a letter to your landlord. In your letter:
• describe the problem and how long it has existed
• explain how it is affecting you
• say what you want the landlord to do
topics.description: IELTS General Writing Task 1 — Semi-formal Letter. Reporting a heating problem to a landlord.
topics.source: Recurring real-exam letter scenario — ieltsbuddy.com latest writing topics
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS General Writing Task 1 Semi-formal Letter to a landlord about a heating problem. Give a band score and feedback on tone, clarity, and bullet coverage.
Write a model Band 7 semi-formal letter of around 170 words that is firm but polite, with a clear request and deadline.
List semi-formal phrases for complaining politely, describing inconvenience, and requesting action.
teacherNotes: Difficulty: Medium — semi-formal register (known recipient, serious matter) is the hardest register to judge.
The tone should escalate politely: problem → impact → clear expectation with a timeframe.
Avoid aggressive language; firmness comes from specifics, not emotion.

topics.topicName:
You recently bought a product online, but when it arrived it was damaged and the seller's customer service was unhelpful.

Write a letter to the company. In your letter:
• describe what you bought and what was wrong with it
• explain what happened when you contacted customer service
• say what you want the company to do
topics.description: IELTS General Writing Task 1 — Formal Letter. Complaint about a damaged online purchase.
topics.source: Recurring real-exam letter scenario (2026) — writing9.com General Task 1 letter bank
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS General Writing Task 1 Formal complaint letter about a damaged online order. Give a band score and feedback.
Write a model Band 7 formal complaint letter of around 170 words with a clear chronology and a specific resolution request.
List formal complaint phrases: 'I am writing to express my dissatisfaction', 'I would appreciate a full refund', 'failing that'.
teacherNotes: Difficulty: Medium — complaint letters test formal register plus narrative sequencing.
Bullet 2 needs a mini-narrative: when you contacted them, what they said, why it was unhelpful.
Bullet 3 should state a primary request plus a fallback (refund or replacement).

topics.topicName:
Your local council is planning to close a public library in your area due to budget cuts.

Write a letter to the council. In your letter:
• explain why the library is important to the community
• describe the consequences of closing it
• suggest an alternative way to reduce costs
topics.description: IELTS General Writing Task 1 — Formal Letter. Persuading the council not to close a library.
topics.source: Modelled on official sample letters — ielts.org General Training sample questions
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS General Writing Task 1 Formal persuasive letter to a council about a library closure. Give a band score and feedback on argumentation and formal register.
Write a model Band 7.5 formal letter of around 180 words that argues persuasively with community-level evidence.
List formal persuasive phrases: 'I urge the council to reconsider', 'this would disproportionately affect', 'a more viable alternative'.
teacherNotes: Difficulty: Hard — persuasive letters to authorities require argumentation skills closer to Task 2.
Consequences should cover different groups: children, elderly residents, students, job seekers.
The alternative suggestion must be realistic and budget-related, not vague.

topics.topicName: Some people think that students should study a foreign language with classmates from different countries rather than with people from their own country. Do you agree or disagree?
topics.description: IELTS Task 2 Agree/Disagree Essay — Language learning with international classmates.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS Writing Task 2 Agree/Disagree essay. Give a band score (0-9) and detailed feedback on Task Achievement, Coherence, Lexical Resource, and Grammar.
Write a model Band 6.5 answer for this question with a clear introduction, two supporting body paragraphs, and a conclusion.
List 10 key vocabulary items and 5 useful sentence structures for this topic.
teacherNotes: Essay type: Agree/Disagree — students must state and maintain a clear position throughout.
Key focus: explain WHY studying with international classmates helps or does not help language learning.
Band 6 target: clear topic sentences, cohesive devices, avoid repetition of the same ideas.

topics.topicName: Some people believe that school children should be given homework every day, while others think that homework is unnecessary. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
topics.description: IELTS Task 2 Discussion Essay — Daily homework for school children.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS Writing Task 2 Discussion Essay. Give a band score and feedback on Task Achievement, Coherence, Lexical Resource, and Grammar.
Write a model Band 6.5 answer: one paragraph for each view, then a paragraph with your own opinion, plus intro and conclusion.
List 10 key vocabulary items and 5 useful expressions for discussing homework and education.
teacherNotes: Essay type: Discuss Both Views + Opinion — students must cover BOTH sides before giving their own view.
Common mistake: only writing one side. Remind students the structure is view A / view B / opinion.
Useful language: advocates of..., critics argue that..., from my perspective...

topics.topicName: Online learning is becoming increasingly popular. Do the advantages of online learning outweigh the disadvantages?
topics.description: IELTS Task 2 Advantages-Disadvantages Essay — Online learning.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS Writing Task 2 Advantages-Disadvantages essay on online learning. Give a band score and detailed feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 answer arguing that the advantages outweigh the disadvantages, with intro, two body paragraphs, and conclusion.
List 10 key vocabulary items and useful phrases for discussing online education.
teacherNotes: Essay type: Outweigh — students must take a clear stance (advantages > disadvantages or vice versa).
Tip: do not simply list pros and cons; compare and show which side is stronger.
Topic link: pairs well with working from home topic for extended vocabulary practice.

topics.topicName: Some people think that all young people should attend university. Others believe that vocational training is more suitable for some students. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
topics.description: IELTS Task 2 Discussion Essay — University vs vocational training.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS Writing Task 2 Discussion essay on university versus vocational training. Give a band score and feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 answer presenting both sides and concluding with a supported personal opinion.
List vocabulary and phrases for comparing university education and vocational training.
teacherNotes: Essay type: Discuss Both Views + Opinion — must acknowledge university benefits AND vocational strengths.
Encourage students to use specific examples (e.g., trade skills, engineering degrees).
Watch for Band 5 trap: writing only about one side instead of both.

topics.topicName: Some people believe that children should start learning a foreign language at primary school rather than secondary school. Do the advantages outweigh the disadvantages?
topics.description: IELTS Task 2 Advantages-Disadvantages Essay — Early foreign language learning.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS Writing Task 2 essay on early foreign language learning. Give a band score and detailed feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 answer arguing that starting a foreign language at primary school has more advantages than disadvantages.
List 10 vocabulary items and useful phrases for this topic.
teacherNotes: Essay type: Outweigh — students must decide whether early learning is overall beneficial or harmful.
Key arguments FOR: brain plasticity, accent acquisition, confidence building.
Key arguments AGAINST: curriculum overload, lack of qualified teachers, potential stress.

topics.topicName: Many people spend too much time using smartphones. What problems can this cause? What solutions can you suggest?
topics.description: IELTS Task 2 Problem-Solution Essay — Excessive smartphone use.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS Writing Task 2 Problem-Solution essay on smartphone overuse. Give a band score and feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 answer: one paragraph on problems, one paragraph on solutions, with intro and conclusion.
List 10 vocabulary items and useful phrases for discussing smartphone addiction and digital wellbeing.
teacherNotes: Essay type: Problem-Solution — students must identify specific problems AND offer realistic solutions.
Problems: social isolation, reduced attention span, sleep disruption, neck/eye strain.
Solutions: screen time limits, digital detox, educational apps, parental controls.

topics.topicName: Social media has changed the way people communicate with each other. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?
topics.description: IELTS Task 2 Advantages-Disadvantages Essay — Social media and communication.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS Writing Task 2 essay on social media. Give a band score and detailed feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 answer arguing that social media has more advantages than disadvantages for communication.
List 10 key vocabulary items and phrases for writing about social media and digital communication.
teacherNotes: Essay type: Outweigh — students should weigh advantages vs disadvantages and state a clear overall position.
Advantages: instant global communication, reconnecting with old friends, sharing information quickly.
Disadvantages: misinformation, reduced face-to-face interaction, privacy concerns, cyberbullying.

topics.topicName: More people are working from home because of modern technology. Do you think this is a positive or negative development?
topics.description: IELTS Task 2 Positive/Negative Development Essay — Working from home.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS Writing Task 2 essay on remote working. Give a band score and detailed feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 answer arguing this is mostly a positive development, with balanced acknowledgement of drawbacks.
List vocabulary and expressions for discussing remote work, productivity, and work-life balance.
teacherNotes: Essay type: Positive/Negative — students must take a clear stance and support it consistently.
Positive points: flexibility, no commute, better work-life balance, environmental benefits.
Negative points: isolation, blurred home/work boundaries, reduced collaboration.

topics.topicName: Children are spending more time using electronic devices and less time playing outdoors. Why is this happening? Is this a positive or negative development?
topics.description: IELTS Task 2 Cause + Evaluation Essay — Children, screens, and outdoor play.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS Writing Task 2 essay on children and screen time. Give a band score and feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 answer: one paragraph on causes, one paragraph evaluating whether this is positive or negative.
List vocabulary and phrases for discussing children, technology use, and physical activity.
teacherNotes: Essay type: Two-part question — students must answer BOTH why it is happening AND whether it is good or bad.
Causes: engaging digital content, safety concerns about outdoor play, parental convenience.
Evaluation: mostly negative (obesity, social skill loss) but some positives (educational apps, digital literacy).

topics.topicName: Some people believe that governments should invest more money in public transport rather than building new roads. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
topics.description: IELTS Task 2 Opinion Essay — Public transport investment vs road building.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS Writing Task 2 Opinion essay on public transport. Give a band score and detailed feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 answer largely agreeing that public transport is a better investment, acknowledging some role for roads.
List 10 vocabulary items and phrases for discussing transport policy and urban planning.
teacherNotes: Essay type: To What Extent — students should express a clear degree of agreement (fully/largely/partially).
Arguments for public transport: reduces congestion, lowers emissions, more cost-effective long-term.
Arguments for roads: necessary for rural areas, supports freight and economic activity.

topics.topicName: Plastic waste is becoming a serious environmental problem in many countries. What are the causes of this problem? What measures can be taken to solve it?
topics.description: IELTS Task 2 Cause-Solution Essay — Plastic waste pollution.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS Writing Task 2 Cause-Solution essay on plastic waste. Give a band score and detailed feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 answer: one paragraph on causes, one paragraph on solutions, with intro and conclusion.
List vocabulary and expressions for discussing plastic pollution, recycling, and environmental policy.
teacherNotes: Essay type: Cause-Solution — students must clearly link specific causes to corresponding solutions.
Causes: excessive packaging, single-use culture, lack of recycling infrastructure, low environmental awareness.
Solutions: plastic bans, producer responsibility laws, public education campaigns, biodegradable alternatives.

topics.topicName: Some people think that individuals cannot do much to protect the environment and that only governments and large companies can make a difference. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
topics.description: IELTS Task 2 Opinion Essay — Individual vs government responsibility for the environment.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS Writing Task 2 Opinion essay on environmental responsibility. Give a band score and feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 answer partially disagreeing: acknowledge that governments and companies have the greatest impact, but argue individuals also play an important role.
List vocabulary and phrases for discussing environmental responsibility at different levels.
teacherNotes: Essay type: To What Extent — a partially agree/disagree position is often the strongest approach here.
Individual actions: reduce consumption, recycling, choosing eco-friendly products, voting for green policies.
Government/company role: legislation, clean energy investment, banning harmful practices.

topics.topicName: Some people think that a high salary is more important than job satisfaction. Do you agree or disagree?
topics.description: IELTS Task 2 Agree/Disagree Essay — Salary vs job satisfaction.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS Writing Task 2 Agree/Disagree essay on salary versus job satisfaction. Give a band score and feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 answer disagreeing: argue that job satisfaction is ultimately more important than a high salary.
List vocabulary and phrases for discussing work motivation, career choices, and personal fulfilment.
teacherNotes: Essay type: Agree/Disagree — students must commit to one side throughout the essay.
Arguments for salary: financial security, ability to support family, reducing stress from debt.
Arguments for job satisfaction: mental health, long-term motivation, sense of purpose.

topics.topicName: Many people find it difficult to achieve a balance between work and personal life. Why does this happen? What can people do to achieve a better balance?
topics.description: IELTS Task 2 Cause-Solution Essay — Work-life balance.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS Writing Task 2 Cause-Solution essay on work-life balance. Give a band score and feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 answer: one paragraph explaining why this problem occurs, one paragraph suggesting practical solutions.
List vocabulary and phrases for discussing work-life balance, stress management, and time management.
teacherNotes: Essay type: Two-part question — students must address both WHY and WHAT TO DO.
Causes: demanding work culture, technology blurring boundaries, financial pressure, lack of employer flexibility.
Solutions: setting clear boundaries, flexible working, prioritising leisure, employer wellness programmes.

topics.topicName: Some people choose to live and work abroad after graduating from university. Do the advantages of this decision outweigh the disadvantages?
topics.description: IELTS Task 2 Advantages-Disadvantages Essay — Living and working abroad.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS Writing Task 2 essay on working abroad. Give a band score and detailed feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 answer arguing the advantages of working abroad outweigh the disadvantages.
List vocabulary and phrases for discussing immigration, career development, and cultural adaptation.
teacherNotes: Essay type: Outweigh — students must take and defend a clear position on balance of advantages/disadvantages.
Advantages: better career prospects, higher income, cultural experience, language skills.
Disadvantages: separation from family, cultural shock, recognition of foreign qualifications.

topics.topicName: In many countries, people are working longer hours than before. Why is this happening? Is this a positive or negative development?
topics.description: IELTS Task 2 Cause + Evaluation Essay — Increasing working hours.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS Writing Task 2 essay on longer working hours. Give a band score and detailed feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 answer: one paragraph on reasons, one paragraph arguing this is mostly a negative development.
List vocabulary and phrases for discussing work culture, productivity, and employee wellbeing.
teacherNotes: Essay type: Two-part question — answer BOTH the cause and evaluation parts clearly.
Causes: economic pressure, competitive job markets, technology making workers always reachable, career ambition.
Evaluation: largely negative (burnout, health problems, family impact) but some argue it drives economic growth.

topics.topicName: Some people prefer living in large cities, while others think that the countryside is a better place to live. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
topics.description: IELTS Task 2 Discussion Essay — City life vs countryside living.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS Writing Task 2 Discussion essay on city versus countryside living. Give a band score and feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 answer: one paragraph on the appeal of city life, one on countryside life, then a personal opinion paragraph.
List vocabulary and phrases for comparing urban and rural environments.
teacherNotes: Essay type: Discuss Both Views + Opinion — all three parts (view A, view B, own opinion) must be present.
City advantages: job opportunities, services, entertainment, connectivity.
Countryside advantages: clean air, lower cost of living, community, peaceful environment.

topics.topicName: Young people today exercise less than previous generations. Why is this happening? What solutions can be introduced?
topics.description: IELTS Task 2 Cause-Solution Essay — Declining physical activity among young people.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS Writing Task 2 Cause-Solution essay on youth inactivity. Give a band score and feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 answer: one paragraph on causes, one paragraph on solutions, with intro and conclusion.
List vocabulary and phrases for discussing exercise habits, sedentary lifestyles, and public health.
teacherNotes: Essay type: Cause-Solution — link each cause logically to a relevant solution.
Causes: screen time, academic pressure, urban environments with few green spaces, passive entertainment.
Solutions: mandatory school PE, subsidised gym access, urban park development, digital fitness apps.

topics.topicName: Advertising encourages people to buy products that they do not really need. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
topics.description: IELTS Task 2 Opinion Essay — Advertising and unnecessary consumption.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS Writing Task 2 Opinion essay on advertising. Give a band score and feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 answer largely agreeing that advertising manipulates consumer behaviour, while acknowledging its informational role.
List vocabulary and expressions for discussing advertising, consumer behaviour, and materialism.
teacherNotes: Essay type: To What Extent — students should express how strongly they agree or disagree, not just list ideas.
Arguments to agree: psychological manipulation, creating artificial desires, planned obsolescence culture.
Arguments to disagree: advertising also informs, promotes competition, and supports free media.

topics.topicName: International tourism has become more popular in recent years. Do the benefits of international tourism outweigh its drawbacks?
topics.description: IELTS Task 2 Advantages-Disadvantages Essay — International tourism.
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS Writing Task 2 essay on international tourism. Give a band score and detailed feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 answer arguing that the benefits of international tourism outweigh its drawbacks.
List vocabulary and phrases for discussing tourism, cultural exchange, and environmental impact.
teacherNotes: Essay type: Outweigh — students must argue that overall, one side is more significant than the other.
Benefits: economic growth for host countries, cultural exchange, funding for heritage preservation.
Drawbacks: environmental damage (carbon emissions, overcrowding), cultural commercialisation, local price inflation.

topics.topicName: Some people believe that university education should be free for all students. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
topics.description: IELTS Task 2 Opinion Essay — Free university education for all.
topics.source: Reported real exam question (2025-2026) — compiled by ieltspodcast.com and ieltsmaterial.com
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS Writing Task 2 Opinion essay on free university education. Give a band score and detailed feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 answer with a clear position, two body paragraphs, and a conclusion.
List vocabulary for discussing tuition fees, public funding, and access to education.
teacherNotes: Difficulty: Easy — familiar topic with accessible arguments on both sides.
Agree: equal opportunity, social mobility, an educated workforce benefits everyone.
Disagree: taxpayer burden, devalued degrees, funds could target the genuinely needy via scholarships.

topics.topicName: Some people think that it is more effective for students to study in a group, while others believe that they should study alone. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
topics.description: IELTS Task 2 Discussion Essay — Group study versus studying alone.
topics.source: Reported real exam question (2025-2026) — compiled by ieltspodcast.com
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS Writing Task 2 Discussion essay on group versus individual study. Give a band score and feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 answer: one paragraph for each view, then a clear personal opinion.
List vocabulary for comparing learning styles: 'peer support', 'distraction-free', 'collaborative skills', 'self-discipline'.
teacherNotes: Difficulty: Easy — concrete, personal topic suitable for early Task 2 practice.
Group study: motivation, sharing knowledge, soft skills; Alone: focus, own pace, deep concentration.
The opinion can be conditional: 'it depends on the task' is fine if clearly argued.

topics.topicName: Recycling household waste should be made a legal requirement. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
topics.description: IELTS Task 2 Opinion Essay — Compulsory recycling laws.
topics.source: Recurring environment topic (2026 rotation) — ieltsliz.com topic list
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS Writing Task 2 Opinion essay on compulsory recycling. Give a band score and feedback.
Write a model Band 6.5 answer taking a clear stance on legally required recycling.
List environment vocabulary: 'landfill', 'household waste', 'enforcement', 'environmental awareness', 'incentives'.
teacherNotes: Difficulty: Easy — environment is one of the most frequent Task 2 themes (~18% of questions).
Agree: voluntary schemes have failed, laws change habits, urgent environmental need.
Disagree: hard to enforce, education and incentives work better than punishment.

topics.topicName: Some people think that robots are very important for humans' future development. Others, however, think that robots are a dangerous invention that could have negative effects on society. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
topics.description: IELTS Task 2 Discussion Essay — Robots: vital for progress or a dangerous invention.
topics.source: Reported real exam question (2025-2026) — compiled by ieltsmaterial.com
samplePrompts: Evaluate this IELTS Writing Task 2 Discussion essay on robots in society. Give a band score and feedback.
Write a model Band 7 answer discussing both views with concrete examples (manufacturing, healthcare, job displacement).
List technology vocabulary: 'automation', 'labour-saving', 'job displacement', 'autonomous systems', 'human oversight'.
